svg.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Expanding Volume
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Expanding Volume; subtitle: Four buckets form a $20,000 planning stack, with matched $5,000 lean and $40,000 expanded allocations.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are the four segments of one $20,000 startup budget. The lean and expanded amounts in each stage use the same 30%, 20%, 30%, and 20% allocation weights and total $5,000 and $40,000 respectively. These are alternative cash plans, not three budgets to add together or scorecard revenue scenarios. Startup cash is not a recurring annual expense total.; caption: Reserve deployment follows evidence, not inbox count. The $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range requires a separate cash forecast, especially because the first deal may take one to four months.; stages: label: Infrastructure and operating systems; value: Plan $6,000; lean $1,500; expanded $12,000 for infrastructure.; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Allocate thirty percent to CRM setup, authorized domains, authenticated mailboxes, scheduling, telephony configuration, and initial subscription cash. Record prepaid services separately from recurring monthly expense.; label: Data and qualification development; value: Plan $4,000; lean $1,000; expanded $8,000 for qualification.; numeric value: 4000.0; detail: Allocate twenty percent to permitted data sourcing, account verification, qualification scripts, and small-sample quality review. Avoid buying broad lists before validating territory fit and contact eligibility.; label: Pilot delivery and acquisition; value: Plan $6,000; lean $1,500; expanded $12,000 for pilots.; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Allocate thirty percent to contractor pilot work and operator-funded acquisition tests. Measure held and accepted appointments rather than opens or raw booked meetings; stop cohorts with unaffordable rejection costs.; label: Working-capital reserve; value: Plan $4,000; lean $1,000; expanded $8,000 as reserve.; numeric value: 4000.0; detail: Retain twenty percent for collection delays, replacement work, and service continuity. The planning reserve covers two months at $2,000 monthly operating spend but only one-third of a month at $12,000.

rect.title: label: Infrastructure and operating systems; numeric value: 6000.0; value: Plan $6,000; lean $1,500; expanded $12,000 for infrastructure.; detail: Allocate thirty percent to CRM setup, authorized domains, authenticated mailboxes, scheduling, telephony configuration, and initial subscription cash. Record prepaid services separately from recurring monthly expense.

Avoid buying broad lists before validating territory fit and contact eligibility.
